content.user_title: Explore Local Receipt Tracking With Manifest V3
content.value_statement: Planning browser receipt capture requires clear storage, extraction, and maintenance requirements. This public guide outlines a local-first extension concept without supplying implementation files.
actual_capabilities: Describes capturing purchase details from browser order-confirmation pages.
Outlines a Manifest V3 architecture using a service worker, local storage, and a popup dashboard.
Names Amazon, Shopify, and WooCommerce as intended merchant targets.
Explains an intended vanilla JavaScript, HTML, and CSS workflow without bundlers.
Lists maintenance constraints, including merchant DOM changes and manual extension reloads.
limitations: The package contains only SKILL.md; extension source, scripts, and templates are absent.
It cannot capture receipts, render a dashboard, or install a working extension by itself.
Local-only storage, merchant support, and Chrome compatibility claims cannot be verified without implementation files.
No automated tests are included, and the guide anticipates manual scraper maintenance.

use_cases.title: Define Personal Receipt-Tracking Requirements
use_cases.description: Identify desired purchase fields and local-storage requirements before selecting or building a receipt tracker.

use_cases.title: Scope a Browser Extension Project
use_cases.description: Use the documented architecture and maintenance constraints to prepare an implementation backlog without assuming source files are included.

use_cases.title: Assess Privacy Claims
use_cases.description: Separate stated local-only design goals from behaviors that require source inspection and runtime verification.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize the Guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize what this receipt-tracking guide describes and identify which implementation files are missing.

prompt_templates.title: Define Receipt Requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the guide to draft requirements for saving merchant names, items, totals, and dates locally. Separate documented goals from verified capabilities.

prompt_templates.title: Plan the Extension Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a Manifest V3 implementation plan from this guide. Cover merchant detection, a service worker, local storage, dashboard views, and manual testing.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Verification Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a verification plan for a future implementation covering permissions, network traffic, local storage, merchant DOM changes, and receipt classification.

output_examples.input: Can I load this package into Chrome as a working receipt tracker?
output_examples.output: No. This package contains a guide only. The extension source and manifest needed for installation are not included.

output_examples.input: What should my implementation backlog include?
output: Define receipt detection and extraction requirements for each intended merchant.
Design local persistence and a spending-history popup.
Inspect permissions and verify network behavior before making privacy claims.
Plan manual checks for merchant page changes and extension reloads.

output_examples.input: Does the guide prove my purchases remain on my device?
output_examples.output: No. It describes local-only storage, but implementation files and runtime evidence are absent. Privacy guarantees require separate verification.

best_practices: Confirm which files are actually present before requesting installation or deployment.
Treat merchant support and privacy statements as design goals until source inspection and runtime testing confirm them.
Use sanitized receipt samples when planning extraction and maintenance tests.
anti_patterns: Claiming the extension was initialized when the package contains no extension source.
Assuming local-only storage is verified because the guide advertises it.
Treating named merchant platforms as tested integrations without implementation evidence.

faq.question: Does this package include a working Chrome extension?
faq.answer: No. The opening notice states that extension source, scripts, and templates are not included.

faq.question: What can I use the guide for?
faq.answer: Use it to discuss receipt-tracking requirements, extension architecture, and maintenance considerations.

faq.question: Which merchants does the guide mention?
faq.answer: It names Amazon, Shopify, and WooCommerce as intended targets. This package provides no detector code to verify support.

faq.question: Does the intended design require a bank connection?
faq.answer: The guide describes reading browser confirmation pages instead of connecting bank accounts. No implementation is included to verify that design.

faq.question: Are local storage and privacy guarantees verified?
faq.answer: No. The guide states those goals, but confirming them requires extension source, permission review, and runtime testing.

faq.question: What maintenance does the guide describe?
faq.answer: Merchant DOM changes may require manual scraper updates. The guide also notes manual developer-mode reloads and the absence of automated tests.
